newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Removed tumour from Swiss minister malignant.
newsitem.headline: Removed tumour from Swiss minister malignant.

text.p: A liver tumour removed from Swiss Economics Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz last week was malignant, the ministry said on Tuesday.

Doctors at Lausanne's University Hospital were not planning any follow-up treatment as the cancerous tumour had been fully removed and had not spread to other parts of Delamuraz's body, a ministry spokesman said.
He said it was impossible to say whether the cancer could return.
"There is a certain risk that the cancer can return, but he could also be healed," the spokesman said.
Delamuraz, 61, who left the hospital on Tuesday, caused international uproar when he described Jewish demands for quick compensation to Holocaust survivors as blackmail.
The spokesman said it was uncertain when Delamuraz would return to work.
Delamuraz's blackmail remark, which stirred angry protests from international Jewish groups, came in an interview with Swiss newspapers in December, 1996.

He said that any compensation by Switzerland to Jews, who might be entitled to money left in Swiss banks after World War Two, should await findings of a panel investigating the country's role during the Nazi era.
Delamuraz later apologised for his remarks, saying they had been based on inaccurate information given to him.
